dossier.public_summary: The 0.95-day dips show a strong odd-even depth difference, V-shaped grazing eclipses, and depths that change by more than half between sectors and from transit to transit. Together this matches a close grazing eclipsing stellar binary at twice the folded period better than a planet.

reasons.why: Strong odd/even depth difference at 4.936 sigma indicates primary and secondary eclipses of an eclipsing binary at twice the folded period, not identical planetary transits.
Highly V-shaped, grazing transit shape with impact parameter near 1 favours a stellar eclipse over a flat-bottomed planet transit.
Depth changes by 54.33% between sectors and sector_depths_by_source verdict is changes_within_a_source (p_constant_all: 2.109026746640543e-08), inconsistent with a stable planet depth.
Individual transit depths are highly inconsistent with a single depth, including a 4.4 sigma outlier at 31323 ppm, supporting variable binary eclipses.
Independent classifier trained on follow-up outcomes rates as strongly non-planet, consistent with binary evidence.
